messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: [OT] examples of good and bad graphic practice
parts:
Hi,

I'm compiling examples for a talk on producing scientific graphs in physics and chemistry. I will present 'the good, the bad, and the ugly' as a means of introduction to best practices and mistakes to avoid when making a plot, regardless of the tool being used. Maybe I'll have a few slides with the original bad graph, and a proposed improvement next to it. Of course being a ggplot2 user, I only have vague memories of truly bad and ugly graphics. Would you have a link to share presenting such examples, along the lines of Tufte's books but online?

Things that come to mind in no particular order,

- 3D pie chart
- some 2D pie charts
- 3D barplots
- double-axis
- misleading axes, and scales
- inappropriate colours
- ugly fonts
- useless "decorations" such as shadows, background image, etc.
- uninformative legend
- plot with too much information (wrong type of plot)
- export in lossy jpeg format
- manual tweaking of data points / scales


Cheers, and a Happy New Year!

baptiste

Some of the Martin Krzywinski talks you can find on http://circos.ca/tutorials/course/ (I think it is session 1) includes various examples of bad graphics taken from the literature - They mostly fall in the 'unnecessary decoration' and 'low data-to-ink ratio'

Happy New Year

Thomas
